Hi Alyssa — thanks for the heads up and the context. Appreciate the advanced notice on your internal calendar shift.

We can definitely avoid a service interruption while Procurement settles on Net60. Two pragmatic options that are operationally quick on our side:

1) Short-term bridge + monthly sweep: Ventra prepays a rolling deposit equal to one monthly expected invoice (we can estimate from your usage for April) and Redwood offsets May invoices against that deposit. When your payment cadence normalizes, the deposit can either be returned or re-applied as the initial reserve for future months.

2) Conditional Net60 with credit guardrails: Approve Net60 for 90 days while we hold a capped credit line (suggested: $250k) and require an approved credit application + two trade references. If overdraft occurs, we trigger an automated billing hold and outreach.

On VAT: for EU-registered entities we support reverse-charge handling on invoices (we can zero-rate VAT if you provide VAT IDs and the correct cross-border documentation). We'll need the EU entity name, VAT ID, and a billing address to apply reverse-charge.

I copied Markus (sales lead) and Neha (finance) so they can weigh in on thresholds and credit docs. If you want, I can draft a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) that lists whichever option you prefer and the exact deliverables (deposit amount, credit app, invoice sweep dates).

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz

Vanessa — thanks for the proposals. Procurement preference is option 2 (conditional Net60) given cashflow constraints, but we are open to a hybrid: a small rolling deposit (one-half month) plus Net60 on net usage. Two conditions we need:

2) A defined credit cap and an automated notification 14 days before hitting 80% of that cap.

Also: since Ventra has an EU-managed services arm, any invoices to our EU company must be processed with reverse-charge where applicable. Please state on each EU invoice the VAT ID and reference the reverse-charge article.

We will circulate our vendor credit application and two references by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks — appreciate the clarity. Proposed commercial guardrails from Redwood: 

- Credit cap: $250,000 (can be revisited after 3 months of on-time payments).
- Rolling deposit: optional 0.5x monthly invoice as a buffer for first 60 days.
- Invoice cadence: monthly invoices on the 5th for prior-month usage; payment due Net60 from invoice date for accounts on Net60.
- Early-pay discount: 1.5% if paid within 15 days (applies to balances settled early).
- Triggers/Notifications: automated email at 14 days before reaching 80% of cap; account team alert at 90%.

If Procurement supplies the credit application and two references, our finance team can typically approve within 3 business days. Legal flagged only one item: we must document the deposit handling and the reversal mechanism in a short amendment to the master services agreement (MSA).
